div.head: Hn 33.2
div.ab: Iniusto quoque iudicio contradici poterit wemminge maiori et sapienciori, presertim si in reddicione fuerit aduocatum.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 564–565 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

Corrected November 2026: the words from “illam reformare” to the end of the sentence, printed by Liebermann at the top of p. 565, with his footnotes a and 1–5 on that page, had been put by mistake at the end of Hn 33.2 when the page was transcribed. They continue the sentence of 33.2a (“Si uero sine calumpnia recipiatur, et deinceps causam illam reformare quis cupiat, non procedet …”), as Liebermann’s own note in vol. III, p. 321 (“33, 2a procedit”) confirms, and are given there now.

Vgl. Gl Urteilschelte 4—6. In Agsächs. Zeit ist dieser Sinn noch nicht belegt. Es heisst (ge)wemman ‘beflecken, tadeln’, (ge)wemming ‘Schändung, Profanation’, gewemmednys dass., gewemmodlice: ‘corrupte’, unwemme(d), -mlic ‘fleckenlos, untadelig, rein, unverletzt’, unwemnes ‘Reinheit’.—Contradicere, chalonger hat diesen Sinn in Frankreich; Brunner II 357.—wemunga—redic.{47}—33, 2a procedit{2} in sceleribus, ut Rs

Cf. Gl Urteilschelte 4—6. This meaning is not yet attested in the Anglo-Saxon period. (ge)wemman means ‘to stain, to blame’, (ge)wemming ‘defilement, profanation’, gewemmednys the same, gewemmodlice: ‘corrupte’, unwemme(d), -mlic ‘spotless, blameless, pure, unharmed’, unwemnes ‘purity’.—Contradicere, chalonger has this meaning in France; Brunner II 357.—wemunga—redic.{47}—33, 2a procedit{2} in sceleribus, ut Rs

div.ab: An unjust judgment, too, can be contradicted by wemminge (impeachment [?]) to the greater and wiser, especially if it was challenged at the rendering.
